Frazier is perhaps best remembered for his fearless 15-round match against Muhammad Ali at Madison Square Garden, known as the Fight of the Century, where he knocked out Ali. In 2011, Frazier passed away from his final fight of liver cancer. Early Years The youngest of 12 children, boxer Billy Joe Frazier was born on January 12, 1944, in Beaufort, South Carolina. His parents, Rubin and Dolly Frazier, were sharecroppers, so the family never had much money. By the age of 15, Frazier, who'd quit school two years before, was on his own. He moved to New York City to live with an older brother and find work. Employment, however, was hard to come by, and to put cash in his pocket he started stealing cars and selling them to a junkyard in Brooklyn. But Frazier harbored dreams of doing something with his life. Many of those dreams were built around boxing. As a younger kid, back in South Carolina, he had dreamed of becoming the next Joe Louis, airing out punches at burlap bags he'd filled with leaves and moss. Up north Frazier's love for boxing didn't subside. After moving to Philadelphia, Frazier found work at a slaughterhouse, where he routinely punched sides of beef stored in a refrigerated room. That scene later inspired Sylvester Stallone for his 1976 film, Rocky. It wasn't until 1961, though, that Frazier entered the ring and actually began to box. He was rough and undisciplined, but his unpolished talent caught the eye of trainer Yank Durham. Professional Career Under the direction of Durham, who shortened Frazier's punches and added power to his devastating left hook, the young boxer quickly found success. The 1968 Olympic champion shared several children with his first wife, Adrienne Calhoun, to whom he was married from 1971 to 1974, per the U.S. Sun . His children with Calhoun include his oldest daughter, Michi Foreman , and his oldest son, George Foreman Jr. After his divorce from Calhoun, Foreman welcomed a daughter named Georgetta with his girlfriend, Charlotte Gross. Foreman’s second marriage was to Cynthia Lewis, and lasted from 1977 to 1979. The pair didn’t have any children together. Nor did the boxer have any kids with his third wife, Sharon Goodson. In 1982, Foreman married his fourth wife, Andrea Skeete, according to Today . Foreman had two children with Skeete, a daughter and a son. Men’s journal says Foreman and Skeete’s daughter, Freeda, died by an apparent suicide at age 42, and reported on the heartbroken message Foreman penned after her death. Sugar Ray Leonard Estimated net worth: $120 Million Sugar Ray Leonard is considered one of the greatest fighters of all time. He won a gold medal at the 1976 Olympics before turning professional, becoming a key figure in boxing’s golden era of the 1980s and winning world titles in five weight classes. He had legendary rivalries with Roberto Durán , Thomas Hearns , Marvin Hagler , and Wilfred Benítez . His victories over these Hall of Famers, including the famous “No Más” rematch against Durán and his controversial decision win over Hagler , solidified his legacy. He retired multiple times but always returned for high-profile fights, finally stepping away in 1997. Since then, he has remained a prominent boxing analyst, commentator, and motivational speaker. 2 7. Lennox Lewis Estimated net worth: $140 Million Lennox Lewis is a former undisputed heavyweight champion, and widely regarded as one of the greatest heavyweights of all time. He won a gold medal at the 1988 Olympics before turning professional. He won multiple world titles throughout the 1990s and early 2000s, defeating legends, and his rivalry with Mike Tyson culminated in a historic 2002 fight, where he won by knockout. He retired as champion in 2004, making him one of the few heavyweights to walk away at the top. He has since worked as a boxing analyst and remains an influential figure in the sport. Sugar Ray Leonard is an American retired professional boxer and motivational speaker who has a net worth of $100 million. Like the original "Sugar Ray" Robinson, Sugar Ray Leonard is considered to be one of the best boxers of all time. Over the course of his 20-year career, he won world titles in five different weight divisions. He also won lineal championships in three different weight divisions and the undisputed welterweight title. After the popularity of heavier fighters like Muhammad Ali faded away, Leonard and three other fighters known as the "Fabulous Four" kept boxing interesting and made fans excited about the lower weight classes. The other four boxers were Roberto Duran, Thomas Hearns , and Marvin Hagler. Leonard succeeded in defeating all three contemporaries, and he also famously beat Wilfred Benitez. Leonard is also famous for his financial success . He became the first boxer to earn more than $100 million in purses. Sugar Ray also won a number of awards , including Boxer of the Year. Sugar Ray Leonard is an American retired professional boxer and motivational speaker who has a net worth of $100 million. Like the original "Sugar Ray" Robinson, Sugar Ray Leonard is considered to be one of the best boxers of all time. Over the course of his 20-year career, he won world titles in five different weight divisions. He also won lineal championships in three different weight divisions and the undisputed welterweight title. After the popularity of heavier fighters like Muhammad Ali faded away, Leonard and three other fighters known as the "Fabulous Four" kept boxing interesting and made fans excited about the lower weight classes. The other four boxers were Roberto Duran, Thomas Hearns , and Marvin Hagler. Leonard succeeded in defeating all three contemporaries, and he also famously beat Wilfred Benitez. sources.excerpt: Mike Tyson's Net Worth in 2025: From Peak Fortune to Financial Rebound Skip to content Search for: Home Entrepreneurship Mike Tyson’s Net Worth in 2025: From Peak Fortune to Financial Rebound Mike Tyson’s net worth stands at approximately $30 million as of 2025, bolstered significantly by his $20 million payout from the November 2024 exhibition fight against Jake Paul on Netflix . This figure reflects a recovery from multiple bankruptcies, including a 2003 filing with $23 million in debt, after earning over $430 million from boxing purses and endorsements during his career. sources.excerpt: --> Smokin' Joe Frazier | The Humble Heavyweight top of page January 12, 1944  -  November 7, 2011 "I HIT HIM WITH BODY SHOTS THAT WOULD'VE BROUGHT DOWN CITIES" SMOKIN' JOE FRAZIER BIOGRAPHY Who Was Joe Frazier?  Joe Frazier was the world heavyweight-boxing champion from 1970 - 1973. Frazier is perhaps best remembered for his fearless 15-round match against Muhammad Ali at Madison Square Garden, known as the Fight of the Century, where he knocked out Ali. In 2011, Frazier passed away from his final fight of liver cancer. Early Years The youngest of 12 children, boxer Billy Joe Frazier was born on January 12, 1944, in Beaufort, South Carolina. His parents, Rubin and Dolly Frazier, were sharecroppers, so the family never had much money. By the age of 15, Frazier, who'd quit school two years before, was on his own. He moved to New York City to live with an older brother and find work. Employment, however, was hard to come by, and to put cash in his pocket he started stealing cars and selling them to a junkyard in Brooklyn. But Frazier harbored dreams of doing something with his life. Many of those dreams were built around boxing. As a younger kid, back in South Carolina, he had dreamed of becoming the next Joe Louis, airing out punches at burlap bags he'd filled with leaves and moss. Up north Frazier's love for boxing didn't subside. After moving to Philadelphia, Frazier found work at a slaughterhouse, where he routinely punched sides of beef stored in a refrigerated room. That scene later inspired Sylvester Stallone for his 1976 film, Rocky. It wasn't until 1961, though, that Frazier entered the ring and actually began to box. He was rough and undisciplined, but his unpolished talent caught the eye of trainer Yank Durham. Professional Career Under the direction of Durham, who shortened Frazier's punches and added power to his devastating left hook, the young boxer quickly found success. He competed from 1965 to 1981. Joe Frazier was famous for his strength, powerful left hand, and constant attacking style. He was also the first boxer to beat Muhammad Ali . Frazier was the undisputed heavyweight boxing champion from 1970 to 1973. Before becoming a pro, he won a gold medal at the 1964 Summer Olympics as an amateur. He became a top boxer in the late 1960s. He beat many strong fighters like Jerry Quarry and Oscar Bonavena . In 1970, he became the undisputed heavyweight champion. Then, in 1971, he famously beat Muhammad Ali in a huge fight called the "Fight of the Century". Two years later, he lost his title to George Foreman . Frazier continued to fight, winning some matches and losing a rematch to Ali. His last big fight was in 1975 against Ali, known as the "Thrilla in Manila". It was a very tough fight for both boxers. Frazier retired in 1976 after losing to George Foreman again. He tried a comeback in 1981 but fought only once more. He finished his career with 32 wins, 4 losses, and 1 draw.
